shippingNews.postTitle: Disabled Freighter Begins Dead-ship Tow Across Lake Superior

stories.body: SUPERIOR, WI – More than two years after sustaining a cracked hull while carrying a load of iron ore pellets and then limping into port, an aging Great Lakes freighter today began a “dead ship tow” across Lake Superior - reportedly so she can be scrapped, maritime sources say. Tug Massachusetts arrives to assist with Michipicoten tow. [Colin Rice] Ship enthusiasts have been eagerly following news of the Michipicoten’s final journey. That trip began today. todayInHistory.title: Millions Spent Restoring Historic Day Peckinpaugh. Now it’s Barely Afloat
todayInHistory.text: The 259-foot Day Peckinpaugh, once envisioned as a floating museum, is in disrepair and could be sunk if its owner can't secure funding Day Peckinpaugh partially submerged. [Times Union] ERIE CANAL – The Day Peckinpaugh, built at Duluth and which once sailed the lower Great Lakes, rests partially submerged in the Hudson River just off the eastern shore on Friday, in Verplanck. The State Museum invested $4 million to restore the historic Erie Canal barge before auctioning it to a private buyer for $5,050 in late 2024. A legendary 259-foot-long motorship that once benefited from millions of dollars in state restoration funding is showing little more than its topside these days. Photographs obtained by the Times Union show the Day Peckinpaugh sitting just above the shallow waters of the Hudson River near a marina in the Westchester County hamlet of Verplanck. The images confirm the vessel’s current condition and location, which had drawn attention last week after a photograph was posted on the boat blog Tugster. Years after the State Museum invested $4 million to restore the ship, the state auctioned it off to private hands for just $5,050 in late 2024. The buyer, Capt. Dwayne Reith, confirmed that the photographs circulating online are authentic. Reith, head of Custom Marine in Dobbs Ferry, said the ship’s steel hull plates are in poor condition and its interior floods constantly. Day Peckinpaugh at Cleveland in 1995. todayInHistory.title: The McKee Sons’ Story is One of Ingenuity and Family Involvement
todayInHistory.text: Rob Alway writes about the laker McKee Sons and the key role the McKee family has played in Great Lakes shipping in his Great Lakes Boat Blog. McKee Sons in 1974. [Roger LeLievre] MUSKEGON, MI – On a recent visit to Muskegon, Michigan, I had the opportunity to tour one of the most interesting vessels remaining on the Great Lakes, a ship that began her life serving the United States during World War II, was transformed into a Great Lakes bulk carrier, and later became a self-unloading barge. The McKee Sons has been docked at Muskegon’s historic Mart Dock for nearly 12 years. Although she has not carried cargo since 2012, the vessel remains a remarkable example of American shipbuilding and the ingenuity of the Great Lakes maritime industry. The ship also represents nearly a century of the McKee family’s involvement in Great Lakes shipping and the ingenuity of its members. My guide for the visit was Patrick McKee, vice president of Sand Products Corp., the family-owned Muskegon company that owns the vessel through its Lake Service Shipping division. Lake Service Shipping’s only vessel is the McKee Sons. PART ONE: From troop transport to lake freighter: The remarkable journey of the McKee Sons. Read the story here PART TWO: Freighter to barge: The McKee Sons’ second life: Read the story here . PART THREE: A century of McKee family maritime history on the Great Lakes: Read the story here .

marineWeather.synopsis: A 29.4 inch low currently centered south of Lake Erie pushes east of the Lower Great Lakes today. Meanwhile, a 29.5 inch Clipper low over Saskatchewan deepens to 29.4 inches over Lake Winnipeg by this evening. The eastern low will then track to Canadian Maritimes at 29.2 inches Saturday while the Clipper low deepening to 29.3 inches over the Manitoba/Ontario line. This low moves over Hudson Bay Sunday night as a 29.5 inch low swings from the OK Panhandle to the Lower Great Lakes. By Monday evening, 30.2 inch high pressure will be south of the Great Lakes, building to 30.3 inches over much of the East Coast Tuesday evening through Wednesday as troughing develops over the Plains.

Low pressure around 29.3 inches is tracking over the eastern Great Lake through remainder of today. While, widespread gales have diminished, cannot rule out sporadic and infrequent northerly gusts to around gales to linger through the remainder of the morning across the southern half of Lake Michigan. Then as wind shift more northwesterly, they are expect to weaken a bit but still remain breezy through tonight. Then expect winds across Lake Michigan to shift more southwesterly for Saturday as two low pressures develop across northern Canada and another across the Central Plains into Sunday. As the southern low pressure deepens to around 29.5 inches and lifts northeastward up the Ohio River Valley, expect gusty west to northwesterly winds to develop across the Lake through the start of next week. Depending on the track and strengthen of this southern low pressure will determine if another potential for gales across southern Lake Michigan will be possible later Sunday as colder air pushes across the region.

marineWeather.synopsis: A potent low pressure system, 29.50 inches, turns toward the eastern Great Lakes today offering gradual improvements to wind speeds and wave heights across the central Great Lakes. Pockets of rain fill back in at times, until this evening. Some showers are possible Saturday, followed by the next low pressure system, 29.40 inches, and cold front early next week.

A low pressure system 29.40 inches will continue to move northeast towards Maine into Saturday. A weak ridge averaging 29.80 inches will build north on Saturday through Saturday night before another low pressure 29.40 inches move east across the region Sunday into Monday moving a cold front east. High pressure 30.20 inches will return on Tuesday.

A 29.5 inch low over Pennsylvania will make its way to the Canadian Maritimes while deepening to 29.2 inches through tonight. A ridge averaging 29.9 inches over the western Great Lakes will then build eastward across the lake Saturday night and Sunday morning, before exiting east into New England Sunday. A 29.6 inch low will deepen to 29.0 inches as it tracks from the Ohio Valley to New England Sunday night and Monday, with a 30.2 inch high then forecast to build across the Lower Great Lakes on Tuesday.
